newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam floods kill 27, leave thousands homeless.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam floods kill 27, leave thousands homeless.

text.p: At least 27 people died and tens of thousands were left homeless by heavy flooding in Vietnam's central provinces at the end of last week, the state-controlled daily Vietnam News said on Tuesday.
There had previously been only sketchy and conflicting media reports of deaths and damage caused by the low tropical atmospheric depression, which brought torrential rains and high winds.
Officials at the Central Committee for Flood and Storm Control were not available for comment on the disaster.
But the Vietnam News quoted the committee as saying that 10 people had died in Ha Tinh, five in both Quang Tri and Thua Thien-Hue, four in Quang Nam-Da Nang and three in Binh Dinh.
Kare Berge of the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies in Hanoi said he had been told by local officials that 17 people died in Ha Tinh.
He said 10,000 hectares (24,700 acres) of the province's rice fields had been destroyed and material damage was estimated at $1.27 million.
Vietnam News said efforts to fly relief supplies by helicopter to Ha Tinh's mountainous Huong Khe district had failed because of poor visibility.
The district, where six people were reported to have died after 15 houses collapsed, was eventually reached by a convoy over land.
The lastest disaster took to around 420 the number of people who have died in tropical storms and flooding in northern and central Vietnam since the beginning of July.
Vietnam suffers a string of floods and storms every year, most between July and October. Officials say damage to northern areas of the country this year has been the worst in a decade.
Storms and flooding usually arrive in the Mekong Delta, the country's southern rice bowl, about the end of September.
